## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readr, writexl)
here::i_am(
  "02_Differential_Expression/03_Protein_Association/a_script/03_protein_association.qmd"
)
```

## Read proteins and phenotype

`proteins` holds the normalised log2 abundances (`E`), the sample table (`targets`) and the gene
annotation. `phenotype.csv` holds one row per leg with muscle size (cross-sectional area, CSA) and
echo intensity, before and after training, for vastus lateralis (`vl_`) and rectus femoris (`rf_`).

```{r read}
stage <- here("02_Differential_Expression", "03_Protein_Association")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
targets <- proteins$targets
values <- proteins$E
phenotype <- read_csv(here("00_Input", "phenotype.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

dim(values)
head(phenotype)
```

## Pair the samples

Each leg has a sample before training (T1) and after (T2). Widening on timepoint gives one row per
leg with both sample identifiers; legs missing either sample are dropped.

```{r legs}
by_timepoint <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  select(leg_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sample_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = sample_id)
legs <- drop_na(by_timepoint, T1, T2) |> arrange(participant, treatment)

nrow(legs)
head(legs)
```

Widening the legs on treatment gives one row per participant with the BFR and HLRT legs side by
side. Participants without both legs drop out.

```{r pairs}
delta_pairs <- legs |>
  select(participant, treatment, leg_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = leg_id) |>
  drop_na(BFR, HLRT)

nrow(delta_pairs)
head(delta_pairs)
```

## Compute changes

The protein change per leg is T2 minus T1 on the log2 scale, one column per leg.

```{r delta}
delta <- values[, legs$T2] - values[, legs$T1]
colnames(delta) <- legs$leg_id
```

The phenotype change per leg is post minus pre for each of the four outcomes. The join is declared
one-to-one because a duplicated phenotype row would silently misalign every leg after it.
Treatment comes from the sample table, so the phenotype file's copy is dropped. Echo intensity
falls as muscle composition improves, so a negative change there is the favourable one.

```{r phenotype-change}
outcomes <- c("vl_csa", "vl_echo", "rf_csa", "rf_echo")
leg_phenotype <- legs |>
  left_join(
    select(phenotype, -treatment),
    by = c("participant", "leg"), relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vl_csa = vl_csa_post_cm2 - vl_csa_pre_cm2,
    vl_echo = vl_echo_post_au - vl_echo_pre_au,
    rf_csa = rf_csa_post_cm2 - rf_csa_pre_cm2,
    rf_echo = rf_echo_post_au - rf_echo_pre_au
  )

head(select(leg_phenotype, leg_id, treatment, all_of(outcomes)))
```

The differential analysis works within participant: BFR change minus HLRT change, for protein and
for each outcome alike. One column per participant.

```{r paired-change}
paired <- delta[, delta_pairs$BFR] - delta[, delta_pairs$HLRT]
colnames(paired) <- delta_pairs$participant
paired_outcome <- map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
  value <- set_names(leg_phenotype[[name]], leg_phenotype$leg_id)
  value[delta_pairs$BFR] - value[delta_pairs$HLRT]
})

dim(paired)
```

## Fit the association

The association is a slope in the same limpa model as `02_Differential`, so it carries the
`dpcQuant()` standard errors. For protein *g* in leg *l* at time *s* (0 before, 1 after):

y(g, l, s) = a(g, l) + s × [b(g, arm) + c(g) × x(l)]

`a` is each leg's own baseline, so only change within a leg counts; `b` is the mean training change
in each arm, so an arm difference cannot pose as association; `x` is the leg's outcome change,
centred on the mean leg. `c(g)` is the extra protein change per unit of extra outcome change, and
its moderated t ranks proteins for gene set tests. Two versions per outcome:

- pooled: the model above, over every leg of both arms;
- differential: one time effect per participant replaces the two arm terms (plus one for BFR), so
  `c(g)` comes only from comparing a participant's two legs.

The paired designs follow the limma User's Guide (sections 9.4.1 and 9.5.3).

```{r samples}
# The one leg without a T2 sample has no outcome change; its x is set to 0, which it never
# multiplies, because its only sample has s = 0.
samples <- targets |>
  mutate(
    leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_"), post = as.integer(timepoint == "T2"),
    bfr_post = post * (treatment == "BFR")
  ) |>
  left_join(select(leg_phenotype, leg_id, all_of(outcomes)), by = "leg_id") |>
  mutate(across(all_of(outcomes), function(x) coalesce(x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 0)))
designs <- list(
  pooled = ~ 0 + leg_id + treatment:post + post:x,
  differential = ~ 0 + leg_id + participant:post + bfr_post + post:x
)
```

Each fit returns the slope, its moderated t, p and the Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) false discovery
rate, within each analysis and outcome.

```{r association-fits}
results <- expand_grid(analysis = names(designs), outcome = outcomes) |>
  pmap(function(analysis, outcome) {
    design <- model.matrix(designs[[analysis]], mutate(samples, x = .data[[outcome]]))
    stopifnot(qr(design)$rank == ncol(design))
    fit <- eBayes(dpcDE(proteins, design, plot = FALSE), robust = TRUE)
    topTable(fit, coef = "post:x", number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
      as_tibble(rownames = "protein") |>
      transmute(
        analysis, outcome, protein, gene = Genes, slope = logFC, t, p = P.Value, fdr = adj.P.Val
      )
  }) |>
  list_rbind()

results |>
  slice_min(p, n = 6) |>
  mutate(across(c(slope, t, p, fdr), function(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

The model has no participant block because a participant's two legs do not correlate in protein
change: the median Spearman r between their BFR and HLRT legs, across proteins, is printed below.

```{r leg-correlation}
leg_r <- map_dbl(rownames(delta), function(id) {
  cor(delta[id, delta_pairs$BFR], delta[id, delta_pairs$HLRT], method = "spearman")
})
round(median(leg_r), 3)
```

`association_t` is the matrix the gene set tests read: one row per protein, one column per
analysis and outcome, values the moderated t.

```{r association-t}
association_t <- results |>
  mutate(column = paste(analysis, outcome, sep = "_")) |>
  select(protein, column, t) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = t) |>
  column_to_rownames("protein") |>
  as.matrix()
dim(association_t)
```

## Hits against chance

A nominal hit is a protein with unadjusted p below 0.05. The chance expectation is the number of
nominal hits expected if no protein were related to the outcome: 5% of those tested. Per analysis
and outcome the table gives proteins tested, nominal hits, the chance expectation, BH hits at 0.05,
the best adjusted p, and the ratio of nominal hits to chance. A ratio near 1 is what no
association at all would produce.

```{r summary}
summary_table <- results |>
  summarise(
    proteins = n(), nominal = sum(p < 0.05), expected = round(n() * 0.05, 1),
    fdr_sig = sum(fdr < 0.05), best_fdr = signif(min(fdr), 3),
    # divide by the exact expectation, not the rounded column above
    ratio = round(nominal / (n() * 0.05), 2),
    .by = c(analysis, outcome)
  ) |>
  arrange(analysis, outcome)
summary_table
```

## Figures

The figures share a theme and an A4 writer.

```{r figure-helpers}
figure_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 6.8, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(3, 3, 4, 3)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
write_pdf <- function(pages, name) {
  pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", name), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
  walk(pages, print)
  invisible(dev.off())
}
```

`association_figure()` draws every nominal hit for one analysis and outcome, smallest p first,
twelve panels to a page. Pooled pages plot each leg's protein change against its outcome change,
with a line fitted inside each arm and the within-arm Spearman r inset. Differential pages plot what
was tested: one point per participant, the BFR minus HLRT difference in protein change against the
same difference in outcome change. Pages are built one at a time from their own rows, because a
paginating facet would build every panel for every page.

```{r association-figure}
association_figure <- function(which_analysis, outcome_name, title) {
  differential <- which_analysis == "differential"
  if (differential) {
    protein_change <- paired
    phenotype_change <- paired_outcome
    point_series <- "BFR - HLRT"
    x_label <- "change in protein, log2, T2 - T1, BFR minus HLRT, one point per participant"
    y_label <- "change in phenotype, BFR minus HLRT"
    headroom <- 0.06
  } else {
    protein_change <- delta
    phenotype_change <- leg_phenotype
    point_series <- leg_phenotype$treatment
    x_label <- "change in protein, log2, T2 - T1, one point per leg"
    y_label <- "change in phenotype"
    headroom <- 0.35
  }
  hits <- results |>
    filter(analysis == which_analysis, outcome == outcome_name, p < 0.05) |>
    arrange(p) |>
    mutate(gene = coalesce(gene, protein))
  points <- pmap(hits, function(protein, gene, outcome, t, p, fdr, ...) {
    arms <- map_chr(c("BFR", "HLRT"), function(arm) {
      keep <- leg_phenotype$treatment == arm
      r <- cor(delta[protein, keep], leg_phenotype[[outcome]][keep], method = "spearman")
      sprintf("%-5s n=%d  r=%+.2f", arm, sum(keep), r)
    })
    tibble(
      panel = sprintf(
        "%s\nvs %s   t = %+.2f   p %s   q %s",
        paste(gene, protein, sep = "  "), outcome, t, signif(p, 2), signif(fdr, 2)
      ),
      change = protein_change[protein, ], d_outcome = phenotype_change[[outcome]],
      series = point_series, inset = if (differential) "" else paste(arms, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)))
  pages <- unname(split(points, (as.integer(points$panel) - 1) %/% 12))
  imap(pages, function(page, i) {
    page <- droplevels(page)
    page_count <- if (length(pages) > 1) sprintf(" (page %d of %d)", i, length(pages)) else ""
    ggplot(page, aes(change, d_outcome, colour = series, fill = series)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_text(
        data = distinct(page, panel, inset), inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = inset), family = "mono",
        hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.25, size = 1.9, lineheight = 1.2, colour = "grey25"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, headroom))) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC", `BFR - HLRT` = "grey25"),
        aesthetics = c("colour", "fill"), name = NULL
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3, nrow = 4, scales = "free") +
      labs(
        x = x_label, y = y_label,
        title = paste0(title, ", ", outcome_name, page_count)
      ) +
      figure_theme
  })
}
```

One PDF per outcome, so each can be read on its own: the pooled pages first, then the
differential ones.

```{r association-pdfs}
walk(outcomes, function(outcome_name) {
  write_pdf(
    c(
      association_figure(
        "pooled", outcome_name, "Training response against phenotype, all legs"
      ),
      association_figure("differential", outcome_name, "BFR minus HLRT, within participant")
    ),
    paste0("03_association_", outcome_name, ".pdf")
  )
})
```

The chance page draws each ratio from the summary as a bar: nominal hits divided by the chance
expectation.

```{r chance-pdf}
#| fig-height: 6
chance_plot <- ggplot(summary_table, aes(ratio, outcome, fill = ratio > 1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%d of %d", nominal, proteins)),
    hjust = -0.12, size = 2.5, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~analysis, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "grey72"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
  labs(
    x = "observed nominal hits / chance expectation", y = NULL,
    title = "Nominal hits relative to chance"
  ) +
  figure_theme +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
write_pdf(list(chance_plot), "03_chance.pdf")
chance_plot
```

## Save results

`03_protein_association.xlsx` holds the summary and every association sorted by FDR;
`04_Protein_Classification` reads the `associations` sheet. `association_t.rds` holds the t matrix
for gene set tests, as rds because a workbook round trip can change the last bit of a double.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(summary = summary_table, associations = arrange(results, fdr))
saveRDS(association_t, file.path(stage, "c_data", "association_t.rds"))
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(stage, "c_data", "03_protein_association.xlsx"))
```
